If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **deceit**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [lips that do not deceive] or [lips that speak truthfully]

nt: Here, **my heart** represents David’s thoughts, feelings, and motives. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my thoughts] or [my inner being]

By **you have visited me in the night**, David means that God examines his heart and thoughts during the quiet hours when his true character is most evident. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [you have examined my heart at night]

Here David is speaking of how people live as if they were actually **paths** that they walk on. The phrase **paths of the violent** refers to living in a way that is characterized by unjust violence against innocent people. (David performed violent actions in the context of war but this refers to non-military violence.) If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a violent way of life] or [a destructive lifestyle characterized by violence]

David is using the adjective **violent** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [violent people]

x.ASV: They have now compassed us in our steps; They set their eyes to cast us down to the earth.
x.Darby: They have now encompassed us in our steps; their eyes have they set, bowing down to the earth.

nt: By **our steps**, David means the steps that both he and his enemies are taking as they move. The enemies are surrounding him at every point along their path. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [They have surrounded me now wherever we go] or [They have surrounded me at every point along our path]

Some ancient manuscripts read **They have surrounded me**. The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts read “They have surrounded us.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

By **Their eyes they have set, crouching down to the earth**, the psalmist means that his enemies are watching him carefully and getting ready to attack him like wild animals that crouch low before they pounce on their prey. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [They stare at me intently, crouched low and ready to attack]

Here David is using imperative forms **Arise**, **confront**, **make him bow down**, and **Rescue** to communicate polite requests to God rather than commands. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please arise, Yahweh, please confront his face, please make him bow down! Please rescue my soul]

Here, **his face** represents his presence or confronting him directly. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [confront him directly] or [face him in battle]

By **make him bow down** David means “throw him to the ground” or “cause him to fall to the ground” and probably means “fall to the ground dead.” You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [make him fall down dead] or [cause him to fall to the ground defeated]

David is using one part of a person, his **soul**, to mean all of him in the act of being rescued. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [me]

David is using the adjective **wicked** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [from wicked people] or [from wicked men]

Here, **sword** represents power or strength used for powerful, violent action. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with your power]
